name: meeple-economy-v1
description: ⭐ THE MEEPLE ECONOMY OF 05/09/2026, WHICH IS THE GAME reference-v14 WAS CUT AGAINST, AND THE ONLY OVERLAY THAT REPRODUCES IT. Written 09/09/2026, when Dean ruled the commons in as the engine default and the meeple economy stopped being the shipped game. Every number in reports/watchlist-2026-09-05T15-25-25-reference-v14.txt was measured on these rules, so without this file the last set of numbers this project quotes would have become unreproducible on the day the default moved. THE STANDING RULE IT SERVES: a branch whose only producer is a knob at its shipped value is not deleted. WHAT IT PINS AND WHY EACH ONE. rules.turn.visitCurrency 'meeple' - a visit costs a MEEPLE placed in the colour slot of a NEIGHBOUR's Notice Board, never your own, and the board is not a building. rules.turn.meepleAsCard true - R15: a meeple of a colour pays wherever a card of that colour would, at a build cost including the n-of-suit and 'any' slots, at a Grow's activation, at a delivery crate; never at a Sow, never at a balloon's move cost. rules.turn.meepleAsCardGoesTo 'board' - R17, and the change that made the second use affordable: the meeple is PLACED on another player's board rather than boxed, and the host collects it. rules.turn.paymentHostChoice 'perPayment' - the whole payment lands on ONE chosen host (Dean ruled per meeple and ruled it back the same day on the branching factor: 25,827 ways to buy one building at four seats against 4,063). rules.turn.paymentSlotToll 1 - the FLAT toll for landing a paid meeple on an occupied slot, however deep. rules.turn.slotToll 1 - the amended R6, and it is PER OCCUPANT rather than flat: visiting a slot holding k meeples costs k extra, all boxed. rules.turn.meepleCapPerColour null - no cap at all, Dean's ruling of 05/09/2026 and the last change the meeple game took. rules.turn.bonusTiming 'end' and rules.turn.startingMeeplesPerColour 1 - PASSENGERS OF THE COMMONS FLIP, pinned here because the shipped defaults moved to 'start' and 0 on 09/09/2026; without them this arm would run the meeple economy with the bonus in the wrong half of the turn and no meeples to start it, which measured a hook of 0.09 the one time anybody tried it. workers.roster.draw.drawUnderMeepleCurrency 2/2 - the Orchard door under the meeple arm, pinned for the same reason. WHAT IT MEASURED, so the arm can be read without opening a report: hook 0.31 rival visits per player per turn; the bonus mix LEVEL for the first time in this project's history, 31.2% rival visit against the empty-board Collect's 30.9%; door mix 29 / 28 / 23 / 12 / 8, the most even ever measured and a PASS; barn glut +1.0, doubled and the first movement in that number across four arms; 2-player blocked-want 8.1%, tripled, which reopened C57; actions per turn 1.31; game 2p 30.0 / 3p 26.5 / 4p 25.1 rounds; verdict 2 PASS / 3 FAIL / 8 OBSERVE. ⚠️ AND WHY IT IS NO LONGER THE GAME, WHICH IS THE ONE THING NO REPORT SAYS: it failed at a TABLE rather than in the simulator. Dean, 09/09/2026 - "with a meeple always available the bonus was basically free". A bonus that is always affordable is not a decision, and every number above was reporting that as a healthy visit rate. READ THAT BEFORE READING ANY OF THEM. ⚠️ THE BOTS ARE NOT THE reference-v14 BOTS. They are whatever the current evaluator is, and nothing re-tunes them when this flag flips, so a per-seat number here is today's opinion of yesterday's rules rather than a replay.
